title: Deficiency Figure Computation — Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Installment Sale Contract
content:
**Recovery Desk terms — the deficiency figure, Kestrel Pre-Owned Retail Installment Sale Contract**

**Definition.** The deficiency figure is the principal balance plus the fees due balance plus interest, rounded to the cent.

- **Interest** is the per diem times the days from the day after the interest-paid-to date through the good-through date.
- **Per diem** is the principal balance times the contract rate divided by the day basis for the tier, rounded to the cent.
- **Good-through date** is the quote validity period for the tier after the quote date.
- **Sale date** is the sale date recorded on the contract.

The interest days are counted in two runs split at the sale date: the days up to and including the sale date, and the days after the sale date through the good-through date. Each run is charged at the per diem and the two amounts are added. Any amount credited against the figure is subtracted from it, and the figure is rounded to the cent once, at the end.

All balances, the contract rate, the interest-paid-to date and the sale date are read from the contract as it stands on the quote date.

### Worked illustration (hypothetical contract)

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| Principal balance | $8000.00 |
| Fees due balance | $600.00 |
| Contract rate | 12.00 percent |
| Day basis | 365 days |
| Days from the day after the interest-paid-to date through the sale date | 20 |
| Days after the sale date through the good-through date | 30 |

Per diem: $8000.00 times 12.00 percent is $960.00 a year; divided by 365 it is $2.6301…, rounded to $2.63. Interest: $2.63 times 20 is $52.60, and $2.63 times 30 is $78.90, together $131.50. Figure: $8000.00 plus $600.00 plus $131.50, that is $8731.50. Every figure in this illustration is hypothetical.
